feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is slightly repetitive, a bit dense, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-focused results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently present a coherent leadership profile in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications.  
- Strong credibility signals: internal progression at NACo, large-scale website migration, team/channel ownership, and specific tools/platforms all reinforce seniority.  
- Good use of metrics and scope: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and channel reach help demonstrate scale.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Add more business outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities or projects well, but more measurable results would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, and could be sharper by foregrounding scale and outcomes.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value statement plus one scope statement; reduce list-like phrasing.
- Add 1–2 proof points from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Replace “Leads” with first-person-neutral phrasing that matches the rest of the CV, e.g. “Specializes in” or “Experienced in leading.”
- Consider rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Brings hands-on leadership across Drupal-based website transformation, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled search—most recently supporting a 10,000+ page platform serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “public-sector communications,” and the capability list repeat the subtitle and Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is vague and overlaps with stronger, more specific wording elsewhere (“AI-enabled search initiative,” “hybrid retrieval”).
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward recent leadership-level strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing nouns, systems, and operations language.
- Emphasize higher-value leadership areas over broad communications wording.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Workflow automation and platform integration • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations • Cross-channel campaign delivery
- If targeting more technical roles, swap “Public-sector advocacy communications” for “CMS and content platform delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills sections, especially governance, analytics, AI search, multimedia, and multi-channel communications.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” is broad and repeats experience bullets without adding new specificity.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce the CV’s themes, but they read a bit dense and overlap with the experience section. Tightening wording and emphasizing outcomes or scope would make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, punchier phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” and trim stacked nouns like “structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat.”
- Add one concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible for 1–2 projects to increase impact.
- Revise for consistency: “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”) and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” if used elsewhere.
- Consider a cleaner format: project name + one-line descriptor, e.g., “AI Hybrid Search — Built a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” adds the most fresh detail; keep that if space is tight.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and name the scope/results where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led enterprise web enhancements spanning CMS/front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and usability improvements for public-facing properties.”
- “Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating detailed project examples already listed in Recent Projects.
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles unless tied to a new result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with solid scale metrics; it should read more like an executive outcomes summary and less like a channel inventory. Emphasize transformation, team/operational leadership, and measurable business impact.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten bullets around outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production cost savings, reporting speed, or governance/compliance improvements.
- Consolidate tools into impact language: “Built an enterprise analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery) to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Video studio/buildout overlaps with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; keep focus here on scale/capability created, not recurring video production.
- “Governance/publishing standards/editorial coordination” repeats prior NACo entries; frame this item as enterprise-wide operationalization.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the earlier Digital Media Manager role and the later Director role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the larger strategic/technical leadership of the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and scalable: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the footer project and 2015–2018 role.
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” risks repeating the governance/standards language in the 2022–2024 Director entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and more differentiated, emphasizing leadership scope and public-sector specialization rather than repeating generic digital/content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “content planning” for a stronger systems-oriented phrase like “content operations” or “publishing workflows.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to scale from recent roles (e.g., enterprise web modernization, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than leaving it fully generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this section high-level and avoid repeating channel lists.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the most recent/high-impact themes: Drupal modernization, integrations/automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long tool list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are target-role priorities; they read as secondary versus recent Drupal-led work.
- Replace “technical execution” with more senior phrasing if desired: “Web Platforms, Integrations & Automation”
- If space allows, add one light qualifier tied to impact, e.g. “supporting large public-facing platforms and content operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies and recent project/work bullets.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-level capability and decision-making impact rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to strategic analytics capability, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • Web performance and SEO analysis • User behavior insights (GA4, Clarity) • BI and data visualization (Looker Studio, Power BI) • BigQuery-based reporting”
- Lead with business outcomes/capabilities, then keep only the most relevant tools in parentheses.
- Replace “optimization” with more specific language like “web performance,” “user behavior insights,” or “decision support.”
- If space is tight, cut one BI tool here and leave the full stack to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact GA4/Clarity/Looker Studio/Power BI/BigQuery sequence elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior and operational, emphasizing production leadership rather than task-level tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and leadership: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” or “Video production leadership” to sound more strategic.
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows: “for advocacy, conferences and recurring digital programming.”
- Keep to 4 concise phrases; use parallel noun phrases and avoid mixing tools with formats unless they signal specialization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”; vary wording or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in recent NACo experience, so this skills line should complement, not repeat, those bullets verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to show depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider replacing “GitHub Pages” with a more relevant platform/tool only if it reflects meaningful recent use; otherwise it can read lightweight versus your enterprise experience.
- Keep ordering impact-based, with Drupal first given repeated recent evidence across current consulting and NACo leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider deleting one version or making this one proficiency-based.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t add that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent projects.
- Use consistent, modern phrasing: spell out “Google Tag Manager (GTM)” if space allows; keep items parallel as tools/capabilities, not mixed formats.
- If possible, add specificity elsewhere in the CV rather than here, e.g., in recent roles: “built front-end components,” “implemented API-driven features,” or “automated deployments with GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions; keep this section tool-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “workflow automation, project tracking, cross-team collaboration”
- Prioritize the most relevant tools tied to recent work; consider dropping Basecamp or Trello if they were not used recently

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this item tool-focused and avoid repeating capability language elsewhere
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less differentiation than Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, or Asana

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership implied by the recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation
- If you’ve used these hands-on recently, prioritize the most current/strategic platform first; if Dynamics was limited exposure, move it after Higher Logic or remove it.
- Add one outcome-oriented qualifier only if defensible, e.g., “supporting newsletters to tens of thousands of stakeholders” or “member communications and lifecycle campaigns.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here if that metric already appears in NACo experience.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t overlap with analytics/optimization tools already listed under Data, Analytics & Optimization.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. It would be stronger if it emphasized methods/capabilities rather than repeating platform names already supported by recent NACo experience.

Suggested edit
- Tighten and group by function: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding”
- Consider renaming to “Analytics, Reporting & Optimization” to sound more outcome-oriented and less tool-list heavy.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “leadership reporting,” since those are evidenced in the 2022–2024 role.
- Keep only the most credible optimization terms; “dashboarding” is weaker than “KPI reporting” or “performance reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; differentiate one as tools and the other as capabilities, or remove one.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director role, so avoid overloading both sections with the same list.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the next NACo roles on workflows, weekly video, and team support. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you can.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add a clearer contribution/result: “Supported a major website refresh and improved cross-channel publishing workflows to increase consistency and speed of delivery.”
- Tighten the content-production line: “Produced livestreams and recurring video content for advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger management phrase only if accurate: “mentored a digital media associate” or “helped supervise a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” duplicates the Associate Communications Director entry; use “recurring video content” here instead.
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with later NACo roles; frame this as helping establish early processes, not leading mature operations.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles that already cover broader content production.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around the clearest achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support statement tied to communications or policy dissemination.
- If possible, add one metric or scope point: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating broad video/content language here; keep this item focused on innovation/research coordination plus the podcast first-launch achievement.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item currently mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the strongest, most current production capabilities implied elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Creative & Audio/Video Tools
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep one capability cue, make it concise: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing
